Update this Next.js application to use Google Cloud Vertex AI with Application Default Credentials (ADC) instead of a Google AI Studio API key (GEMINI_API_KEY or GOOGLE_API_KEY).
Please do the following:
1. Update Dependencies: Replace @google/generative-ai (or update @google/genai) with the official @google-cloud/vertexai SDK (or configure @google/genai with vertexai: true).
2. Remove API Keys: Remove any apiKey initialization parameters from the server-side code (API routes / Server Actions) so the SDK automatically falls back to local Application Default Credentials (ADC).
3. Configure Environment Variables: Replace GEMINI_API_KEY in .env.local and .env.example with GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT and GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION (defaulting to us-central1).
4. Update Model Initialization: Initialize the Vertex AI client using process.env.GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT and process.env.GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION and ensure all Gemini calls run strictly on the server side."
</pasted_content id="5b79">
I'll look at the current Gemini setup and the uncommitted changes already in place.

content.text:
Gemini now runs on Vertex AI using Application Default Credentials (ADC), with no API key anywhere. Typecheck passes, but I haven't made a live call because no Google Cloud project is set yet.

**To make it work locally**, run these, then put your project ID in `.env.local`:
```
gcloud auth application-default login
GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=<your-project-id>
```
Then `node scripts/gemini-smoke.mjs` checks it end to end.

What changed:
- **No new dependency.** I kept `@google/genai` and set `vertexai: true` with project and location, instead of adding `@google-cloud/vertexai`. That's one of the two options you listed, and it means no other code had to change.
- `src/lib/gemini/client.ts` and `scripts/gemini-smoke.mjs` no longer pass `apiKey`. The SDK finds your ADC credentials on its own.
- `src/lib/env.ts`, `.env.example` and `.env.local`: `GEMINI_API_KEY` is replaced by `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` (required) and `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION` (defaults to `us-central1`).
- `SPEC.md` and `docs/hang-notes.md` now describe the new setup.
- **Server-only:** this was already true. The Gemini client imports `server-only`, so the build fails if browser code ever imports it.

The old `GEMINI_API_KEY` in `.env.local` wasn't a real API key. It looked like a short-lived Google sign-in token (it started with `ya29.`), which is probably why it kept failing. It's gone now.

Your earlier changes to `src/lib/http.ts` (the friendly out-of-quota error) are still there. I didn't commit anything.
OMG IT WORKS CAN YOU COMMIT PUSH AND MERGE
I'll follow the repo workflow: check for a trail, run `entire review`, then commit and push.

Run a multi-agent review against the current branch or a --target branch:
several reviewer agents review the change in parallel, then a single judge consolidates their
reports into the final verdict in a closing round. Reviews are saved as named
profiles in Entire settings and clone-local preferences. On first run, guided
setup writes a profile and asks before starting agents.

Flags:
  --configure    set up a review profile (shows available agents + profiles).
                 With --set-* flags it writes the profile non-interactively;
                 otherwise it opens the wizard (interactive) without starting agents.
  --set-agents   with --configure: comma-separated reviewer agents for the profile
  --set-judge    with --configure: the consolidating judge as agent[=model]
  --set-output   with --configure: where the verdict goes: local (default) or trail
  --local        with --configure: save to .entire/settings.local.json (just you)
                 instead of .entire/settings.json (shared). Interactive setup asks.
  --set-task     with --configure: the profile's canonical task text
  --set-model    with --configure: per-reviewer model as agent=model (repeatable)
  --set-slot     with --configure: a reviewer slot as agent[=model] (repeatable;
                 the same agent/model may repeat to run it multiple times)
  --set-config   with --configure: a reviewer's own agent config as
                 reviewer=<config.json|isolated|none> (repeatable). It replaces
                 the reviewed checkout's hooks, MCP servers and extensions; the
                 checkout's skills still load. Saved to clone-local preferences.
  --edit         re-open the advanced profile skill picker
  --findings     browse local findings; pass a handle to print one saved run
  --agent NAME   run only one reviewer from the selected profile
  --list         list configured review profiles (their reviewers and judge)
  --agents       list the reviewer agents you can pass to --agent for the profile
  --model NAME   override the model for the --agent reviewer (requires --agent)
  --models       list the models each agent advertises (optionally --agent NAME)
